title: Rough cleaning

blocks.what_we_do: First we remove [wells](docs/glossary.md#well) that were read very badly. A well is a small hole in a plate that holds the DNA of one sample. Then we remove [variants](docs/glossary.md#variant) (also called sites) that were read very badly. A variant is a place in the DNA where people differ.
blocks.why:
Some wells fail in the laboratory. For these wells, many results are missing. [Missingness](docs/glossary.md#missingness) is the share of [genotypes](docs/glossary.md#genotype) that could not be read. A genotype is the pair of DNA letters that a person has at one site.

Gross failures distort later summaries of missingness and of [heterozygosity](docs/glossary.md#heterozygosity). Heterozygosity means that a person carries two different [alleles](docs/glossary.md#allele) (versions of the DNA letter) at a site.

First, we remove samples with more than 10% missing genotypes. Second, we recompute the missingness of each variant on the samples that remain. Third, we remove variants with more than 10% missingness.

The order matters. Removing poor wells can improve the apparent [call rate](docs/glossary.md#call-rate) of a site. The call rate is the share of genotypes that were read successfully. This step is only a first screen. It is not the final 98% call-rate rule.
blocks.command:
```{r s3-1}
# 1. Choose the input files and the names for the saved files.
input <- guided_path(cfg, "2.8")
rough <- guided_path(cfg, "3.1", "samples")
# 2. Remove samples with more than 10% of calls missing.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", input, "--mind", "0.10", "--make-pgen", "--out", rough))
# 3. Remove variants with more than 10% of calls missing.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", rough, "--geno", "0.10", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.1")))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.1", "2.8")
guided_register(cfg, "3.1", "2.8", 2013, 296360, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-8_state --mind 0.10 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-1_samples --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-1_samples --geno 0.10 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-1_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

There are two separate commands on purpose. The second command works on the samples that survive the first.

`--mind 0.10` removes wells with more than 10% missingness. `--geno 0.10` removes sites with more than 10% missingness in the wells that remain. `--pfile` selects the input fileset in the PLINK 2 native format. `--make-pgen` saves the result as a new fileset (a saved state). `--out` sets the name prefix of the output files. `--threads 2` limits the number of worker threads (parallel jobs). `--memory 2048` sets the memory limit to 2048 MiB (about 2 gigabytes).
blocks.expected_result:
Three wells and 150 variants are removed. 2,013 samples and 296,360 variants remain.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in

blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file named in the message and the previous step. Keep the command and the console messages. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: Failed wells and sites that failed badly. This check cannot tell you the biological or technical cause by itself.
blocks.quick_check:
Why do we recalculate variant missingness after we remove the very poor wells?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Poor wells can make good sites look bad.

</details>
blocks.files_created: `s3-1_samples.*`, `s3-1_state.*`, the lists of removed samples and variants, and the replay metadata (notes that let the course repeat this step).
blocks.try_other_thresholds:
This box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it. It does not change your results.

The step makes a rough first clean. `--mind` is the largest share of missing calls that a sample may have. `--geno` is the same limit for a variant. A low value is strict and removes more. A high value is generous. At 0.10 only wells and sites that are clearly broken are removed. The finer checks come later, at steps 3.2 and 4.1, so this first clean can be generous. Each trial below starts from the same input as the step and changes one threshold only.

```{r s3-1_thresholds, eval=FALSE}
# Optional. Each trial starts from the same input and changes one threshold only. Your results folder is not changed.
thresholds <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
# 1. Samples: --mind on the cohort saved at 2.8.
samples <- threshold_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "2.8"), "--mind", thresholds)
samples$course_value <- samples$threshold == 0.10
samples
# 2. Variants: --geno on the samples that remain after --mind 0.10.
variants <- threshold_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.1", "samples"), "--geno", thresholds)
variants$course_value <- variants$threshold == 0.10
variants
# 3. Plot the removed numbers. The course value is the large diamond.
par(mfrow = c(1, 2)); plot_threshold_trials(samples, "Samples removed"); plot_threshold_trials(variants, "Variants removed")
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```

Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-8_state --mind 0.05 --make-just-psam --out results/trials/s3-1_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The log file `results/trials/s3-1_trial.log` states how many samples were removed. To repeat the trial, change the number after `--mind` and use a new `--out` name. For variants, use `--geno` and `--make-just-pvar`, and start from `results/guided/s3-1_samples`. PLINK 2 treats a dosage without a hard call as missing by default (the `dosage` modifier changes this). The course data have hard calls only, so this makes no difference here.

The expected result of the trials:

Samples removed by `--mind`:

| Threshold | Samples removed | Samples remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.01 | 121 | 1,895 |
| 0.02 | 45 | 1,971 |
| 0.05 | 3 | 2,013 |
| **0.1 (course value)** | 3 | 2,013 |
| 0.2 | 3 | 2,013 |

Variants removed by `--geno`, after `--mind 0.10`:

| Threshold | Variants removed | Variants remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.01 | 3,705 | 292,805 |
| 0.02 | 958 | 295,552 |
| 0.05 | 735 | 295,775 |
| **0.1 (course value)** | 150 | 296,360 |
| 0.2 | 130 | 296,380 |

How to read it. Between 0.05 and 0.20 the same three wells are removed. Those wells are so poor that no limit in this range keeps them. Below 0.05 the limit starts to remove good wells too (45 at 0.02 and 121 at 0.01). For variants, a stricter limit removes many more sites. The course value of 0.10 keeps the rough clean generous on purpose.

Expected plot. For `--geno`, the horizontal axis shows the threshold and the vertical axis shows the number of variants removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.1), where 150 variants are removed. For `--mind`, the horizontal axis shows the threshold and the vertical axis shows the number of samples removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.1), where 3 samples are removed. The line joins the points in the order of the thresholds, so you can see how fast the count changes. The same plot with ggplot2 looks the same and has a light grid.
